content.text: {"verdict":"pass","reasons":["Classification is correct: the § 2(a) grant names only Client, with no affiliate/contractor coverage and no notice mechanism to add them, and § 15 permits assignment only to a financially responsible affiliate with no successor/M&A carve-out — so the clause fails both material elements of the fallback (affiliates on notice; successor transfer), not merely the preferred wording.","Rationale correctly declines walk-away treatment (no at-will revocation; termination tied to uncured breach) and correctly treats the subscription rather than perpetual term as a non-flagged sub-element.","Redline is actionable and reaches the playbook position with a targeted edit: inserts 'its affiliates and its contractors acting on Client's behalf' into the grant and appends a successor/merger/asset-sale carve-out to § 15; the elevated changed-character ratios reflect necessary insertions rather than gratuitous rewriting.","Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, cites the business reason and offers the written-notice fallback, consistent with the required tone and prefix.","Minor, non-blocking: adding affiliates/contractors leaves 'in the ordinary course of its business' slightly ambiguous as to whose business, and the § 15 carve-out is drafted mutually (also benefiting TrueLink) — both acceptable as an opening position."]}

reasons: Classification is correct: the § 2(a) grant names only Client, with no affiliate/contractor coverage and no notice mechanism to add them, and § 15 permits assignment only to a financially responsible affiliate with no successor/M&A carve-out — so the clause fails both material elements of the fallback (affiliates on notice; successor transfer), not merely the preferred wording.

Rationale correctly declines walk-away treatment (no at-will revocation; termination tied to uncured breach) and correctly treats the subscription rather than perpetual term as a non-flagged sub-element.

Redline is actionable and reaches the playbook position with a targeted edit: inserts 'its affiliates and its contractors acting on Client's behalf' into the grant and appends a successor/merger/asset-sale carve-out to § 15; the elevated changed-character ratios reflect necessary insertions rather than gratuitous rewriting.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, cites the business reason and offers the written-notice fallback, consistent with the required tone and prefix.

Minor, non-blocking: adding affiliates/contractors leaves 'in the ordinary course of its business' slightly ambiguous as to whose business, and the § 15 carve-out is drafted mutually (also benefiting TrueLink) — both acceptable as an opening position.
